meta.date: The practice of the church, written out by Moroni after AD 400
meta.unit: The manner of ordaining priests and teachers (Moroni 3)
principles: A wording preserved with the alternative built into it
An office named by what it is for
A calling matched to the man

world_behind.title: The disciples were also called elders
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives both names for the same men. 3 Nephi 19:4 names the twelve and nothing in that book calls them elders, so this verse is where the office name attaches to them in the record.

world_behind.title: Priests and teachers are much older offices
world_behind.text: Jarom 1:11 has prophets, priests and teachers laboring together about four hundred years before Christ, and Mosiah 23:17 has Alma consecrating all their priests and teachers. Verse 1 preserves a form for offices the record has been using for eight centuries.

world_behind.title: Prayer comes first here too
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has them pray to the Father in the name of Christ before the hands go on. Moroni 2:2 puts mighty prayer before the power to give the Holy Ghost, and Moroni 4:2 puts kneeling and prayer before the sacrament.

world_behind.title: The alternative is written into the form
world_behind.text: Verse 3 carries the teacher wording inside a parenthesis. Nothing else in the volume preserves a set of words with a variant printed inside it, which is what a document looks like when it is being copied rather than remembered.

world_behind.title: The criterion has its inventory later in the book
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says they ordained according to the gifts and callings of God unto men. Moroni 10:8 to 17 lists those gifts one by one, seven chapters on.

world_behind.title: The power used is the one granted in chapter 2
world_behind.text: Verse 4 grounds the ordinations in the Holy Ghost the ordainers themselves carried. Moroni 2:2 is where they were given it, so the two chapters are the grant and its exercise, in that order.

words.text: Older men set over a congregation. The record uses the word nine times and the King James Bible a hundred and seventy-nine.
Set apart to an office. Treated at 1 Nephi 12:7. It appears nineteen times in the record and thirty-five in the King James Bible.
Those who officiate. The record uses the word seventy-nine times and the King James Bible four hundred and one.
Those charged with instruction. The record uses the word thirty times and the King James Bible fourteen.
The releasing of a debt or a charge. Treated at 2 Nephi 31:17. Verse 3 puts it beside repentance as what the office is to preach.
Holding on to the end. The word appears twice in the record, here and at Moroni 8:3, and never in the King James Bible.
Summonses to a particular work. The word appears once in the record, here, and never in the King James Bible in this plural.

phrases.term: The disciples, who were called the elders of the church
phrases.text: Two names for one group. Moroni gives the second so the reader can place them.
The two offices this chapter covers. One form of words serves both.

phrases.term: After they had prayed unto the Father in the name of Christ
phrases.text: The step before the hands. Moroni 2:2 set the same order for the disciples themselves.

phrases.term: They laid their hands upon them, and said
phrases.text: The gesture and the speech together. Verse 3 supplies the speech.

phrases.term: In the name of Jesus Christ I ordain you to be a priest
phrases.text: The sentence as spoken. It opens with the name and states the act.

phrases.term: (Or if he be a teacher, I ordain you to be a teacher)
phrases.text: The variant kept inside the quoted form. The record preserves the choice rather than giving two forms.

phrases.term: To preach repentance and remission of sins through Jesus Christ
phrases.text: The charge that comes with the office. The office is defined by the message.

phrases.term: By the endurance of faith on his name to the end
phrases.text: How that preaching is to be carried. The phrase closes the ordination before the amen.

phrases.term: According to the gifts and callings of God unto men
phrases.text: The measure used in ordaining. What a man is given decides what he is ordained to.

phrases.term: They ordained them by the power of the Holy Ghost
phrases.text: What made the ordination effective. Verse 4 says that power was already in the ordainers.
The last clause of the chapter. It puts the source inside the men doing the work.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: The twelve under a working title
verses.text: The heading calls them "the disciples, who were called the elders of the church." The phrase elders of the church appears twice in the volume, here and at Alma 4:16, and this is the only place it is attached to the twelve. The chapter is about office, and it opens by naming one.

verses.label: v. 2–3
verses.title: The rubric is preserved with the prayer
verses.text: The formula carries its own alternate wording inside it: "I ordain you to be a priest (or if he be a teacher, I ordain you to be a teacher)." What the record hands on is not a remembered occasion but a form with instructions for its reuse.

verses.label: v. 4
verses.title: Authority stated twice, two different ways
verses.text: The ordinations went "according to the gifts and callings of God unto men," and they were done "by the power of the Holy Ghost, which was in them." One clause locates the authority in what God gives and the other in what the ordainers already carry. The record sets them side by side and does not rank them.

chapter.title: One chapter covers two offices
chapter.text: Verse 1 names priests and teachers and verse 3 handles both with a single form.

chapter.title: Prayer precedes the hands
chapter.text: Verse 2 puts the asking first, as Moroni 2:2 did for the disciples themselves.

chapter.title: The wording is preserved as spoken
The alternative sits inside the quotation
chapter.text: Verse 3 keeps the teacher wording in a parenthesis, so the reader sees the choice being made.

chapter.title: The office is named by its work
chapter.text: Verse 3 defines it as preaching repentance and remission of sins.

chapter.title: Endurance is written into the charge
chapter.text: Verse 3 asks for faith on his name to the end, in the ordination itself.

chapter.title: The man's gifts set the office
chapter.text: Verse 4 makes the ordaining follow what God has already given him.

chapter.title: The power was in the ordainers
chapter.text: Verse 4 closes by locating the Holy Ghost in the men laying on hands.

applications.title: Record the manner, not only the fact
applications.text: The chapter's stated subject is the manner in which the disciples ordained priests and teachers. Preserving how a thing was done is what lets a later generation repeat it instead of reconstructing it.

applications.title: Say the thing plainly
applications.text: The form of words is short, names the authority, and states the office.

applications.title: Define a job by what it is for
applications.text: The ordination names the work of preaching repentance.

applications.title: Match the work to the gift
applications.text: They ordained according to what God had given the man.

applications.title: The power was already in them
applications.text: They ordained by the power of the Holy Ghost which was in them, and they matched the office to what God had given the man. Nothing in that sentence is borrowed from outside the people doing it.

questions.text: Whom do I look to as an elder, and why?
What am I doing without praying about it first?
Could I say plainly what I have been asked to do?
What would enduring to the end look like this year?
What gift have I been given that I have not put to work?
Am I choosing tasks by what I want or by what I am given?
What am I trying to do on my own power?
